reference.title: Floats
reference.shortdesc: This reference lists the properties that CSSMedia uses to float boxes to the side of their lines, to the edges of a page or of a column, and to wrap text around their shapes.

row.entry: Takes a box out of the normal flow. With float-reference: inline the box goes to the start or the end of its lines and the text wraps beside it: block-start and top go to the start, block-end and bottom to the end, and left and right are the two sides of the line. With a page or a column as reference, the box goes to that edge of the page area or of the column, and the text goes on in the rest. snap-block() and snap-inline() float the box only when it stands within the given distance of an edge; otherwise it stays where it is. footnote makes the element a footnote.

none, left, right, top, bottom, block-start, block-end, inline-start, inline-end, snap-block, snap-block(one or two lengths, and start, end or near), snap-inline, snap-inline(one or two lengths, and left, right or near), or footnote

What the box floats in. inline is its line. page is the page area, and column the column of a multi-column element; outside a column, a column float floats in its line. region floats in the line as well.

Moves a block-level box or a float below the earlier floats on the sides that the value names. both names both sides. left and right are the left and right of the lines, which are the top and bottom in vertical text. inline-start, block-start and top name the side where the lines start; inline-end, block-end and bottom name the side where they end. A value that names the start side also moves the box below an initial letter. On a page or a column float, the value closes that page or column to the later floats that go to the edge it names.
none, left, right, both, inline-start, inline-end, block-start, block-end, top or bottom
CSS 2 §9.5.2; CSS Logical 1 §2.2; CSS Page Floats 3 §4

Moves a page or column float to a later page or column. A positive number counts pages or columns on from the one of the box, up to the last one. A negative number counts back from the last one, and last is the last one.

Moves a page or column float away from the edge it floats to, and from the float before it on that edge. A percentage is of the size of the page area or column less the size of the float, so 50% centers it.

The outline that the lines beside a float or an initial letter wrap around, cut to its margin box. A basic shape is drawn in a box of the float, the margin box when no box is named. An image gives the pixels whose alpha is above shape-image-threshold, stretched over the box. The float is placed by its margin box all the same.

none, a basic shape (inset(), rect(), xywh(), circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), path(), shape()) and a box (margin-box, border-box, padding-box, content-box), either alone, or an image: url(), a gradient, image(), image-set() or cross-fade()
Keeps the lines that far from the shape, still inside the margin box. A percentage is of the length of the lines of the containing block.
A length or a percentage, not negative
The alpha above which a pixel of a shape-outside image is part of the shape.
A number from 0 to 1 or a percentage
